title: Encode sACN discovery universe lists in network byte order
problem: sACN discovery copies bytes directly from an array of state structures, so universe numbers use host byte order and later entries are read at the wrong stride.
reproduce: Encode universes 1, 256 and 0x1234 on a little-endian host; the baseline cannot produce the required 00 01 01 00 12 34 payload.
acceptance: Every discovery universe is selected from its structure entry and encoded as a 16-bit big-endian value.
repair: Replace the raw memcpy with an element-wise network-order serializer and add a byte-exact C regression.

selection.reason: The owner-acknowledged protocol defect has exact byte-level acceptance, no competing PR, and a hardware-free native regression.

verification.limitations: BCL verifies exact discovery payload bytes and builds the sACN backend on Linux. No physical sACN receiver was used.
verification.ownerCheck: Run discovery with multiple configured universes and confirm a receiver lists each expected universe.
